pages.title: Introduction
pages.description: UI สไตล์ macOS สำหรับ Roblox ที่ให้คุณจัดการคอนโทรล ธีม และคอนฟิกได้อย่างเป็นระเบียบ โดยใส่ใจรายละเอียดเล็ก ๆ ของการใช้งาน
pages.markdown:
## เรียบง่ายในทุกครั้งที่เปิด

PearlUI เป็น UI library ฝั่ง client เขียนด้วย Luau มีหน้าต่าง แถบข้าง คอนโทรล และ Dock ที่ทำงานร่วมกัน คุณเป็นคนกำหนด callback และพฤติกรรมของแอป ส่วน PearlUI ดูแลการแสดงผลและการโต้ตอบ

- **8 คอนโทรลหลัก** พร้อม callback และการจัดการค่าผ่าน API
- **9 ธีม** รวม Forest โทนเขียวมืด และการปรับสี Accent
- **2,029 ไอคอน Lucide** เลือกใช้ได้ทุกคอนโทรล แท็บ และ section
- **คอนฟิกแยกตามเกม** เมื่อกำหนด `ConfigScope` ตาม `game.GameId`
- **รันซ้ำได้** ด้วยชื่อเดิม ตัวเก่าจะถูกปิดก่อนสร้างตัวใหม่

## เริ่มจากหน้าต่างเล็ก ๆ

สร้าง ModuleScript ชื่อ `PearlUI` ใน ReplicatedStorage แล้วเรียกจาก LocalScript:

```lua
local PearlUI = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.PearlUI)
local window = PearlUI.new({
    Name = "MyApp",
    Title = "My interface",
    Theme = "Forest",
    ConfigScope = "game_" .. tostring(game.GameId),
})

local tab = window:Tab({ Name = "General", Icon = "house" })
local section = tab:Section({ Title = "Settings", Icon = "settings" })

section:Toggle({
    Id = "enabled", Label = "Enabled", Icon = "power", Default = false,
    Callback = function(value)
        print("Enabled:", value)
    end,
})

local ok, status = window:Ready()
print(ok, status) -- true, Session only
```

## ไปต่อทางไหนดี

อ่าน [Getting started](#/getting-started) สำหรับการติดตั้งจริง หรือเปิด [Showcase](#/showcase) เพื่อดูตัวอย่างทั้งหมด ส่วน [API Reference](#/api) มีเมธอดและผลลัพธ์ที่ตรงกับ implementation

> ไม่มี adapter จะใช้งานและสร้างคอนฟิกภายในหน้าต่างนั้นได้ แต่ยังไม่จำค่าข้ามการรัน อ่านวิธีต่อระบบบันทึกใน [Persistence](#/persistence)

pages.title: Getting started
pages.description: ติดตั้งใน Roblox Studio สร้าง UI แรก และเลือกวิธีบันทึกค่าที่เหมาะกับโปรเจกต์
pages.markdown:
PearlUI 1.0.2 is a client UI library. The application owns gameplay callbacks,
permissions and its choice of storage. Core, bundled icons and session-only use
work without executor APIs or runtime HTTP.

## Roblox Studio

1. Import dist/PearlUI.rbxmx into ReplicatedStorage as ModuleScript PearlUI, or
   copy src/PearlUI.luau into that ModuleScript.
2. Copy examples/Starter.client.luau to a LocalScript in
   StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts. Run Play.
3. Replace callbacks with the app's behavior. Keep explicit stable IDs. Build
   every control before calling Ready.

```lua
local PearlUI = require(game.ReplicatedStorage.PearlUI)
local window = PearlUI.new({
    Title = "My interface", Theme = "Forest",
    ConfigScope = "game_" .. tostring(game.GameId),
})
local tab = window:Tab({Name="General", Icon="house"})
local section = tab:Section({Title="Settings", Icon="settings"})
section:Toggle({Id="enabled",Label="Enabled",Icon="power",Default=false,
    Callback=function(value) print("Enabled:", value) end})
local ok, status = window:Ready()
print(ok, status) -- true, Session only
```

## Retain settings between sessions

Choose one real adapter, then use the same final Ready call:

```lua
local ok, message = window:Ready({
    Adapter = adapter, Key = "my_app", DefaultConfig = "Default",
    AutoSave = true, Load = true, Debounce = 1.5,
    OnStatus = function(status, errorMessage)
        print(status, errorMessage or "")
    end,
})
if not ok then warn(message) end
```

- For your Roblox experience, install src/PersistenceClient.luau in
  ReplicatedStorage as PearlUIPersistence and examples/Persistence.server.luau
  in ServerScriptService. Set adapter to require(PearlUIPersistence). Server
  DataStore access must be configured for the experience. Keep keys <=24 bytes.
  Clients are scoped to the invoking player; they cannot choose another UserId.
- For a compatible local preview, use examples/FileStorage.luau with available
  file functions. The generated standalone demo already integrates it. Core has
  no dependency on those functions. Keep per-app key/folder and per-account prefix.
- Without an adapter the UI is usable and configs work within that window,
  but Ready reports Session only. It does not claim to save across sessions.

Ready captures the construction baseline once, creates Default for fresh data,
then loads storage. Saved current state/auto-load can override constructor values.
It does not automatically start gameplay actions. Failed loading returns false
and blocks writes; surface the error and retry after the adapter recovers. Repeated
successful Ready calls preserve edits. The lower-level CaptureDefaults and
ConfigurePersistence APIs remain available.

## Touch and gamepad

Responsive=true and GamepadNavigation=true are defaults. Phones use a compact
icon rail, readable scale, stacked fields and larger hit areas. The desktop
window geometry is retained for restoration. Set Responsive=false only if the
app supplies its own layout.

Call window:Focus(control) to start navigation. Select enters/refocuses the UI;
A activates, B closes a popup/dialog or hides the window, shoulders change tabs.
Left/right D-pad changes sliders and hue/alpha; the SV area also accepts up/down.
Text entry uses Roblox's native TextBox keyboard. No global navigation setting
is changed, and shortcuts act only while the window owns selection. An app can
opt out with GamepadNavigation=false. System reduced motion is respected.

## Icons, lists and lifecycle

All controls and sections accept Icon; controls/tabs/sections expose SetIcon.
Tab icons update the sidebar and dock. See Icons.md for the complete catalog.
Dropdown PageSize defaults 50 (10–100); search covers all options, while only
one bounded page is built. This includes lists such as all 2,029 Lucide names.

ReplaceExisting defaults to true: rerunning with the same Name and Parent retires
the previous PearlUI window, dock and floating panels before creating a fresh one.
Use a stable Name for each app. A different name or parent creates an independent
interface; ReplaceExisting=false permits deliberate duplicates. Reusing a name does
not transfer session-only values. Use the same adapter and key with Ready to reload
saved state. Overlapping replacements while a save is pending return an error;
retry after the first run finishes. No close confirmation is shown for a rerun.

Call window:Destroy() for an explicit teardown. It disconnects input,
focus listeners, jobs, panels and ScreenGuis. Hide/minimize keeps the instance
and storage watcher alive. Persist=false excludes inspectors and temporary values.
Callbacks run safely with errors reported; handle app errors rather than silently
ignoring failed storage or config operations.

## Delivery and verification

Open dist/PearlUI-Demo.rbxlx for the full Studio showcase, or build with Rojo
using default.project.json. Use dist/PearlUI-Demo.client.luau only in a compatible
client preview. Production deployments can pin a reviewed commit; the core
ModuleScript is the normal Studio integration.

Run python tools/check.py --compiler <path-to-luau-compile> before publishing
changes. Read tests/ReleaseValidation.json for the precise tested surfaces and
remaining manual device checks. Simulated input/viewport tests do not certify
every physical device or a published DataStore deployment.

pages.title: Load from GitHub
pages.description: ตัวอย่างเรียกใช้งานจริงสำหรับ client ที่รองรับ HttpGet และ loadstring พร้อมหน้าต่าง Forest สอง section
pages.markdown:
## เรียกตัวอย่างล่าสุด

โค้ดนี้ดาวน์โหลดตัวอย่างจาก repository ของ PearlUI และโหลด core จาก commit ที่ตรึงไว้ในตัวอย่าง

```lua
local app = loadstring(game:HttpGet(
    "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/emperhub/PearlUi/main/examples/Remote.client.luau"
))()
```

## รันซ้ำได้เลย

ตัวอย่างใช้ `Name = "PearlRemoteExample"` เหมือนเดิมทุกครั้ง จึงแทนที่หน้าต่างเก่า รวม Dock พาแนลย่อย และตัวรับปุ่ม โดยไม่ต้องลบ GUI เอง

## ใช้ handle ที่ส่งกลับมา

```lua
app.Window:SetTheme("Forest")
app.Controls.Message:Set("Hello from PearlUI")
app.Window:Notify({
    Title = "Ready",
    Description = app.Controls.Message:Get(),
    Preview = true,
})

-- เมื่อต้องการปิดจากโค้ดโดยตรง
app.Window:Destroy()
```

## Roblox Studio

Studio ใช้ `require(ModuleScript)` ตาม [Getting started](#/getting-started) ตัวอย่าง HttpGet/loadstring ขึ้นอยู่กับสภาพแวดล้อมที่รองรับ โค้ด core ปกติไม่ต้องใช้ runtime HTTP หรือฟังก์ชันไฟล์ของ executor

ตัวอย่างนี้ไม่มี persistence adapter จึงไม่เปลี่ยนคอนฟิกของตัวทดสอบหลักและไม่จำค่าข้ามการรัน

pages.title: Window
pages.description: สร้างหน้าต่าง จัดขนาด เปิด–พับ และแทนที่ UI เดิมเมื่อรันสคริปต์ซ้ำ
pages.markdown:
## สร้างหน้าต่าง

```lua
local window = PearlUI.new({
    Name = "MyApp", Title = "My interface", Theme = "Forest",
    Columns = 2, Scale = 1, AnimationSpeed = 0.2,
    ToggleKey = Enum.KeyCode.RightShift,
    Responsive = true, GamepadNavigation = true,
    ReplaceExisting = true,
    ConfigScope = "game_" .. tostring(game.GameId),
})
```

`Name` เป็นชื่อที่ใช้จับคู่ UI เมื่อรันซ้ำ ส่วน `Title` เป็นข้อความบนแถบหัว ตั้งชื่อแอปให้คงที่เพื่อให้ตัวเก่าถูกแทนที่อัตโนมัติ

## ปรับขนาดและการแสดงผล

```lua
window:SetSize(900, 610)
window:SetScale(1)
window:SetOpacity(0.97)
window:SetMinimized(true)
window:SetMinimized(false)
window:SetVisible(false)
window:SetVisible(true)
```

ขนาดและ opacity ใช้ setter ไม่ใช่ constructor options ดูค่าทั้งหมดใน [Defaults](#/defaults)

## ปุ่มหน้าต่างสามสี

- **แดง** เปิดคำถามยืนยัน ถ้าตกลงจะปิด UI, Dock และพาแนลย่อยทั้งหมด
- **เหลือง** พับหน้าต่างและใช้ Dock เปิดกลับได้
- **เขียว** สลับขยายเต็มพื้นที่กับขนาดเดิม

กด Cancel, Escape หรือพื้นที่นอกคำถามเพื่อยกเลิก การเรียก `Destroy()` จากโค้ดเป็นการปิดโดยตรง

## รันซ้ำและหลายหน้าต่าง

ค่าเริ่มต้น `ReplaceExisting = true` จับคู่จาก **Name และ Parent** แล้วเรียก teardown ของเจ้าของเดิม แม้เป็นไลบรารีที่โหลดคนละรอบ UI ชื่อต่างกันจะยังอยู่

```lua
-- แทนที่หน้าต่าง MyApp ตัวเดิม
local window = PearlUI.new({ Name = "MyApp" })

-- เฉพาะกรณีตั้งใจให้มีชื่อซ้ำหลายหน้าต่าง
local additional = PearlUI.new({
    Name = "MyApp",
    ReplaceExisting = false,
})
```

การแทนที่สร้างค่าชุดใหม่ ถ้าต้องการโหลดค่าที่เคยบันทึก ใช้ adapter และ key เดิมตอน `Ready()` หากกำลังบันทึกก่อนปิดอยู่ การสร้างซ้ำที่ชนกันจะคืน error เพื่อกัน UI ซ้อน ให้รอรอบแรกเสร็จก่อน

pages.title: Tabs
pages.description: แบ่งพื้นที่ใช้งานด้วยแท็บ ไอคอน และคำอธิบาย โดยสลับแท็บจาก UI หรือโค้ดได้
pages.markdown:
```lua
local general = window:Tab({
    Name = "General", Icon = "house",
    Description = "A place for your everyday settings.",
})
local appearance = window:Tab({ Name = "Appearance", Icon = "palette" })

window:SelectTab(general)
window:SelectTab("Appearance")
appearance:SetIcon("paintbrush")
```

## ไอคอนบนแท็บและ Dock

`SetIcon()` เปลี่ยนไอคอนทั้งแถบข้างและ Dock โดยยังเก็บแท็บที่เลือกไว้ ใช้ชื่อจาก [Icons](#/icons)

## ตัวควบคุมเกมแพด

เมื่อหน้าต่างเป็นเจ้าของ selection แล้ว ใช้ shoulder buttons เปลี่ยนแท็บได้ ส่วน `Focus(control)` พาไปยังคอนโทรลที่ต้องการ อ่านรายละเอียดใน [Getting started](#/getting-started)

pages.title: Sections
pages.description: จัดคอนโทรลเป็นกลุ่ม วางซ้าย–ขวา และแยก section เป็นหน้าต่างลอย
pages.markdown:
## สร้าง section

```lua
local settings = general:Section({
    Id = "general.settings", Title = "Settings",
    Icon = "settings", Column = "Left",
})
local feedback = general:Section({
    Id = "general.feedback", Title = "Feedback",
    Icon = "bell", Column = "Right",
})
settings:Toggle({ Id = "enabled", Label = "Enabled", Default = false })
```

## จัดคอลัมน์

`window:SetColumns(2)` ใช้สองคอลัมน์เมื่อพื้นที่เพียงพอ เมื่อพื้นที่แคบจะยุบเป็นหนึ่งคอลัมน์ ใช้ `Column = "Left"` หรือ `"Right"` ระบุด้าน และใช้ Id ที่คงที่เมื่อบันทึก layout

## แยกและคืนพาแนล

```lua
settings:Detach()
settings:Reveal()
settings:Dock()
settings:SetIcon("folder-open")
```

`Dock()` คืนเนื้อหากลับ section ต้นทางทันที แล้วค่อยเฟดกรอบลอยที่ว่างออก ดูรายละเอียดใน [Panels & dock](#/panels)

pages.title: Panels & dock
pages.description: ย้าย section ออกมาลอย ลาก Dock ซ่อนด้านข้าง และเปิดกลับสู่ตำแหน่งใช้งาน
pages.markdown:
## พาแนลลอย

```lua
local section = general:Section({ Id = "tools", Title = "Tools" })
section:Button({ Label = "Example", Text = "Run", Callback = function()
    print("Running")
end })

section:Detach() -- แยกออกจากหน้าหลัก
section:Reveal() -- เปิดและโฟกัสพาแนลที่แยกแล้ว
section:Dock()   -- คืนไปยังหน้าเดิม
```

## Dock และการกู้คืน

Dock เริ่มที่กึ่งกลางด้านบน ลากย้ายและนำไปซ่อนขอบซ้ายหรือขวาได้ ปุ่มเหลืองพับหน้าต่างโดยยังเหลือ Dock ส่วนปุ่มแดงปิดทั้งหมดหลังยืนยัน

```lua
window:SetMinimized(true)
window:StowDock("Left")
window:RevealDock()
window:SetMinimized(false)
```

## เก็บ layout

```lua
local layoutJSON = window:ExportLayout()
local ok, message = window:ImportLayout(layoutJSON)
if not ok then warn(message) end
```

การเก็บ layout เป็น JSON ยังไม่ใช่การบันทึกลงไฟล์หรือ DataStore ด้วยตัวมันเอง ใช้ [Persistence](#/persistence) เพื่อเก็บข้ามครั้ง

pages.title: Notifications
pages.description: แจ้งผลลัพธ์จาก callback หรือทดลองแจ้งเตือนแม้ผู้ใช้ปิดการแจ้งเตือนปกติ
pages.markdown:
```lua
window:Notify({
    Title = "Settings updated",
    Description = "Your changes have been applied.",
    Duration = 4,
})

-- ปุ่ม Preview ต้องแสดงผลได้แม้ notifications ถูกปิดไว้
window:Notify({
    Title = "Notification preview",
    Description = "This is how your notifications look.",
    Preview = true,
})
```

## ค่าการแจ้งเตือน

`window.NotificationsEnabled = false` ระงับการแจ้งเตือนปกติ ส่วน `Preview = true` ข้ามค่านี้เฉพาะครั้งนั้น โดยไม่เปลี่ยน preference ที่เก็บไว้

pages.title: Confirmation
pages.description: ขอคำยืนยันก่อนทำสิ่งที่มีผลต่อค่า หรือแสดงข้อความให้ผู้ใช้เลือกทำต่อ
pages.markdown:
## สร้างคำถาม

```lua
local question = window:Confirm({
    Title = "Apply changes?",
    Description = "Your current settings will be replaced.",
    ConfirmText = "Apply",
    OnConfirm = function() print("Confirmed") end,
    OnCancel = function() print("Cancelled") end,
})
```

## ควบคุมจากโค้ด

```lua
question:Cancel()
-- หรือ question:Confirm() เมื่อโค้ดตั้งใจให้ยืนยัน
```

Handle ทำงานได้เพียงครั้งเดียว กดซ้ำหลัง Confirm/Cancel แล้วไม่ทำ callback ซ้ำ การเปิด dialog ใหม่จะยกเลิกตัวเก่า

## รีเซ็ตด้วยคำถามยืนยัน

เรียก `Ready()` หรือ `CaptureDefaults()` หลังสร้างคอนโทรลให้ครบ ก่อนใช้ `RequestReset()`

```lua
window:RequestReset("Appearance")
-- scopes: Appearance, Controls, Layout, All
```

ปุ่มแดงใช้ confirmation ก่อนปิดทั้ง UI อยู่แล้ว ไม่ต้องเขียนคำถามปิดหน้าต่างซ้ำ

pages.title: Themes
pages.description: เลือกจาก 9 ธีมในตัว หรือกำหนด Accent ของแอปเองโดยยังเปลี่ยนธีมได้
pages.markdown:
## เลือกธีม

```lua
local names = PearlUI.GetThemes()
window:SetTheme("Forest")
window:SetTheme("Dark")
```

## กำหนด Accent

```lua
window:SetAccent(Color3.fromRGB(110, 180, 140))
window:SetTheme("Midnight") -- สีที่ตั้งเองยังคงอยู่
window:ResetAccent()        -- กลับไปตามสี Accent ของธีม
window:SetTheme("Forest")
```

`SetAccent()` เลือกโหมด Custom ส่วน `ResetAccent()` คืนโหมด Theme และตามสีของธีมถัดไป ปุ่มสลับสว่าง–มืดบนเว็บนี้เปลี่ยนเฉพาะคู่มือ ไม่เปลี่ยน UI ใน Roblox

## ค่าเริ่มต้น

constructor เริ่มจาก **Light** ตัวอย่างบน GitHub และ Starter เลือก **Forest** ไว้โดยเจตนา ดูตารางสีทั้งหมดใน [Defaults](#/defaults)

pages.title: Icons
pages.description: Lucide 2,029 ไอคอนในตัวไลบรารี ค้นหาชื่อหรือ alias แล้วคัดลอกไปใช้ในโค้ดได้ทันที
pages.markdown:
## ใส่ไอคอนใน UI

```lua
local tab = window:Tab({ Name = "General", Icon = "house" })
local section = tab:Section({ Title = "Tools", Icon = "settings" })
local toggle = section:Toggle({
    Id = "enabled", Label = "Enabled", Icon = "shield-check",
})

toggle:SetIcon("power")
tab:SetIcon("layout-dashboard")
section:SetIcon("folder-open")
```

## ชื่อและ alias

ใช้ kebab-case เช่น `shield-check` เป็นรูปแบบที่อ่านง่าย ตัวไลบรารีรองรับชื่อ PascalCase, underscore และ prefix `lucide:` ด้วย รายชื่อจริงอยู่ใน `PearlUI.Icons` และ alias ใน `PearlUI.IconAliases`

ไอคอนถูกแพ็กใน core แล้ว จึงไม่ต้องดาวน์โหลดรูปทีละตัวใน Roblox สิทธิ์และต้นทางดูใน [Icons guide](https://github.com/emperhub/PearlUi/blob/main/docs/Icons.md) และ [Lucide license](../assets/lucide/LICENSE)

pages.title: Configs
pages.description: สร้าง บันทึก โหลด เปลี่ยนชื่อ และนำเข้า–ส่งออกคอนฟิก โดยแยกรายชื่อกับค่าล่าสุดตามเกม
pages.markdown:
## เริ่มต้นคอนฟิก

สร้าง UI และคอนโทรลทั้งหมดก่อนเรียก `Ready()` ใช้ `ConfigScope = "game_" .. tostring(game.GameId)` เพื่อแยก bank ตามเกม

```lua
window:Ready()
local ok, name = window:CreateConfig("My setup")
if ok then print("Created:", name) end
window:SaveConfig("My setup")
window:LoadConfig("My setup")
```

Open **Profiles**. Configs are separated by Roblox game (GameId), with a
separate saved list, last setup, active config and auto-load choice per game.
Places in the same game use the same config scope.

## Everyday use

1. Enter a **Config name** and click **Create** to capture the current setup.
2. Select a name in **Saved configs**. Selection alone does not apply values.
3. Click **Load** to apply it. Edited active configs get a replacement prompt.
4. After changing settings, click **Save changes** to update that named config.
5. Edit the name field and click **Rename** to rename the selected config.
6. **Delete…** asks for confirmation and leaves the live settings unchanged.

The active config displays **saved** or **edited**. Manager fields and switching
tabs or showing/hiding the window do not mark a config edited. Auto-save stores
your latest working setup and config list; it does not silently overwrite a
named config's saved values.

**Auto-load selected** uses that config's saved values next time this game is
opened. With auto-load off, the last working setup for this game is restored.
Rename updates auto-load references; deleting that config clears its auto-load
selection. **Reset all** does not remove your saved configs.

## Share a config

- Select a config and click **Export JSON**. Select and copy its text.
- Enter a name, click **Import JSON…**, paste the text and confirm.
- Invalid JSON stays in the editor with an error. It is not applied or stored.
- Replacing an existing name requires a separate confirmation.
- Import creates a saved copy in the current game. It does not load it
  automatically or change the game scope. Click **Load** when ready.

The export contains one profile with a version, name and source scope. It does
not contain the other configs. Legacy ExportProfile JSON can also be imported.
The editor uses Roblox's [TextBox selection and clipboard support](https://create.roblox.com/docs/reference/engine/classes/TextBox).

## Library API

```lua
local window = PearlUI.new({
    Title = "My UI",
    ConfigScope = "game_" .. tostring(game.GameId),
})
-- Build controls first. UI-only manager fields can use Persist = false.
window:CaptureDefaults()
-- ConfigurePersistence loads banks and applies the chosen startup config.

local ok, nameOrError = window:CreateConfig("Farm")
window:SaveConfig("Farm")
window:LoadConfig("Farm")
window:RenameConfig("Farm", "Gather")
window:SetAutoLoadConfig("Gather")
window:SetAutoLoadConfig(nil) -- disable auto-load for this scope

local names = window:ListConfigs() -- sorted defensive copy
local status = window:GetConfigStatus()
-- status.Scope, status.Active, status.AutoLoad, status.Dirty, status.Count
local json, errorMessage = window:ExportConfig("Gather")
window:ValidateConfig(json)
window:ImportConfig("Shared", json)       -- rejects duplicate names
window:ImportConfig("Shared", json, true) -- explicit overwrite
window:DeleteConfig("Gather")

local listener = window:OnConfigsChanged(function()
    -- Refresh your picker/status labels.
end)
listener:Disconnect()
```

Mutation methods return success plus a normalized name or error. ExportConfig
returns JSON or nil plus an error. ValidateConfig returns success plus any
validation error without changing live values. New names allow 1–32 UTF-8
characters, trim surrounding whitespace and reject control characters and
case-insensitive duplicates. Legacy longer profile names remain loadable.

Each game can hold 20 configs, with at most 32 game scopes in one settings
document. One config is limited to 50 KB; imported transfer text to 100 KB;
the full settings envelope remains limited to 200 KB. Capacity checks reject
before replacing stored values. SaveProfile remains available and uses the
same storage-budget checks.

The settings envelope keeps its existing Version=1, Current and Profiles
fields, adding Configurations.Version=1 and Banks. Each bank stores Profiles,
Current, Active and AutoLoad. Old settings without banks migrate their named
profiles into the first current game scope; their live setup is preserved.
The optional file adapter retains its existing backup/recovery behavior.

pages.title: Persistence
pages.description: เลือกวิธีจำค่าข้ามครั้งผ่าน adapter จริง พร้อมสถานะบันทึก การรีเซ็ต และการกู้คืนเมื่อโหลดไม่สำเร็จ
pages.markdown:
The library accepts a storage adapter and has no dependency on executor file APIs.
The standalone preview includes an optional file adapter. The Studio demo place
includes a server DataStore integration.

## Local preview

Run `dist/PearlUI-Demo.client.luau` in the same local preview environment used
for the demo. When file APIs are available, it uses
`PearlUI/u<LocalPlayer.UserId>_demo.json`, with `.tmp` and `.bak` recovery copies
in that environment's file workspace. The files contain only PearlUI settings
and named profiles. Different account prefixes do not share settings.

An adapter factory is also provided in `examples/FileStorage.luau`. Its file
functions may be supplied through `FileSystem`, so integrations can use their
own storage implementation.

## Your Roblox game

The generated `PearlUI-Demo.rbxlx` already includes:

- `ReplicatedStorage/PearlUI`: the UI module.
- `ReplicatedStorage/PearlUIPersistence`: `src/PersistenceClient.luau`.
- `ServerScriptService/PearlUIPersistenceServer`: `examples/Persistence.server.luau`.
- `StarterPlayer/StarterPlayerScripts/PearlUIDemo`: the client demo.

For an existing game, put those sources in the same locations. The server owns
the `PearlUI_Settings_v1` data store and keys each settings document by the
invoking player's UserId and a short application key. Clients never supply
another player's UserId. Saves require acknowledgement from `UpdateAsync`.

DataStore services must be available for the published experience. Studio
DataStore access is an explicit experience setting; it is not enabled by this
project. The server uses a six-second save cooldown, and the client retries
failed automatic saves while keeping the latest values in memory. A failed
initial load blocks writes until a successful reload, preventing a temporary
read failure from overwriting an existing setup with defaults.

References: [Roblox data stores](https://create.roblox.com/docs/cloud-services/data-stores)
and [RemoteFunction communication](https://create.roblox.com/docs/scripting/events/remote).

## Custom adapter API

Construct controls first, capture defaults, then load storage:

```lua
window:CaptureDefaults()
local ok, message = window:ConfigurePersistence({
    Key = "my-ui", -- server adapter: 1–24 ASCII letters, digits, _ or -
    Adapter = {
        Load = function(key)
            return yourStorage:Read(key) -- JSON string, or nil when absent
        end,
        Save = function(key, json)
            yourStorage:Write(key, json)
            return true -- explicit acknowledgement is required
        end,
    },
    Debounce = 1.5,
    AutoSave = true,
    OnStatus = function(status, errorMessage)
        -- Ready, Loading, Unsaved, Saving, Saved or Error
    end,
})
```

`SaveSettings()` and `LoadSettings()` return success plus an error/result.
`GetPersistenceStatus()` returns the current status and any error.
`DisablePersistence(true)` flushes before disconnecting the adapter;
`DisablePersistence(false)` disconnects without a write. The automatic watcher
checks settings every 0.5 seconds, then waits for the debounce interval after
the last observed edit. `Destroy()` attempts a final save when auto-save is on.
Use **Save now** and wait for **Saved** before leaving if recent changes are
still pending. A process termination or unavailable storage service cannot be
guaranteed to preserve edits that have not yet been acknowledged.

The storage envelope includes per-game config banks and their current control values, appearance, window/tab/
panel/dock layout and named profiles. Usernames, avatar images and transient
notifications are not stored. The maximum settings document is 200,000 bytes.

## Reset controls

`CaptureDefaults()` records the initial setup independently of named profiles.
Mark appearance controls with `ResetGroup = "Appearance"`; other controls
default to the `"Controls"` group.

```lua
window:RequestReset("Appearance") -- confirmation dialog first
window:RequestReset("Controls")
window:RequestReset("Layout")
window:RequestReset("All")
```

`Reset(scope)` applies immediately for code integrations and returns success
plus any validation error. Resetting does not delete named profiles. A general
`Confirm({Title, Description, ConfirmText, OnConfirm, OnCancel})` dialog is also
available; its handle has `Confirm()` and `Cancel()` methods. Escape, Cancel
or clicking outside the dialog cancels without applying the reset.

## Theme accent

`SetAccent(color)` selects a custom accent. `ResetAccent()` or `SetAccent(nil)`
returns to the current theme's accent and follows subsequent theme changes.
New profiles record `Appearance.AccentMode` as `"Theme"` or `"Custom"`.
Older profiles without that field retain their saved custom-color behavior.

The demo's **Appearance → Personalization → Use theme color** button restores
this mode and updates the color picker. Appearance and control resets remain
separate from layout resets.

## Per-game configuration banks

Version 0.7.0 adds separate banks for each ConfigScope while retaining the
existing Version=1 / Current / Profiles envelope. The demo uses GameId to
choose its scope. Both the latest working setup and the named config list
are separate per game. A selected auto-load config overrides that game's
last working setup at startup. Legacy data migrates into the first current
scope and the file adapter retains a backup. See [Configs.md](Configs.md)
for the manager controls, schema and transfer API.

Version 1.0.2. [Machine-readable catalog](../defaults/PearlUI.defaults.json),
[minimal runnable example](../examples/Default.client.luau), [API contract](API.md), [production integration](GettingStarted.md).
The catalog is documentation: do not pass the entire JSON object to `PearlUI.new`
or import it as a saved config. Resolve Enum, Color3 and Parent in Luau.

## Window constructor

| Option | Default | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Title / Name | Pearl UI / PearlUI | Visible title / ScreenGui base name |
| Theme | Light | Forest is the available dark-green theme |
| Accent | nil | Follow the current theme; Color3 selects Custom mode |
| Parent | nil | LocalPlayer.PlayerGui |
| DisplayOrder | 50 | Dock uses this + 1 |
| Columns | 2 | Only 1 or 2; narrow content collapses to one |
| Scale | 1 | Desired range 0.65–1.3; viewport fit can reduce actual scale |
| ReduceMotion | false | App toggle; system reduced-motion preference also bypasses animation |
| Responsive | true | Phone layout below 640px; touch landscape below 500px height |
| GamepadNavigation | true | Scoped selection, focus ring, Back, shoulders and D-pad adjustment |
| ReplaceExisting | true | Retire existing PearlUI windows with the same Name and Parent before creation |
| AnimationSpeed | 0.2 seconds | Effective duration clamps to 0.05–0.6 |
| ToggleKey | Enum.KeyCode.RightShift | Constructor needs Enum, setter accepts string too |
| ConfigScope | global | Demo deliberately uses game_<game.GameId> |

Desktop initial size is 900 × 610; bounds are 680 × 420 through 1440 × 1000.
Initial opacity is 0.97 (range 0.75–1), notifications enabled, visible and
not minimized/maximized. These are runtime state, **not constructor options**:
use `SetSize`, `SetOpacity`, `SetVisible`, `SetMinimized`, `SetMaximized`.
The dock starts at the very top center, up to 330 × 54 with a 22px recovery handle.
On phones it fits within the safe viewport. Mobile fills the available window at
readable scale 0.85–1.1 with a 56px icon rail and 44px touch targets. Desktop size
remains stored for switching back; mobile layout does not rewrite it.
Two-column content threshold is 580 logical pixels; gap 14 and card gap 16.
Corners: window 14, card 12, field 7. Fonts: Gotham/GothamMedium.

## Sections and controls

Tab defaults: Name `Tab`, Description empty, Icon lowercase Name.
Section defaults: Title `Section`, Id `<Tab.Name>.<Title>`, alternating Left/Right,
Icon `grip-vertical`. All controls accept optional Icon; SetIcon(nil) removes it.
Value control Id defaults to `<Tab.Name>.<Section.Title>.<Label>`; prefer explicit
stable IDs. Button and Label have no persisted Id. Common options: Visible true,
Disabled false, Persist true, ResetGroup `Controls`; Description/Callback/reason unset.
Label defaults to the control kind. Set ResetGroup `Appearance` for theme controls.

| Control | Defaults / required values |
|---|---|
| Toggle | Default false |
| Slider | Min 0, Max 100, Step 1, Default Min, Suffix empty |
| Dropdown | Options required, nonempty unique strings; Multi false; Searchable true; PageSize 50 (10–100); first option / empty array for multi |
| ColorPicker | Default current palette Accent, Alpha 1 |
| Input | Default empty, MaxLength 128 UTF-8 characters, Placeholder Enter text |
| Keybind | Default RightShift; OnPressed unset |
| Button | Text Run, Primary false |
| Label | Value empty; string shorthand supported |

Use `Get` for live values and `Serialize` for JSON. ColorPicker Get returns Color3
and alpha; serialization returns `{Hex, Alpha}`. Set(value, true) suppresses the
callback. Disabled controls still accept programmatic Set.

Notify defaults: Title `Done`, Description empty, Duration 4 seconds, Preview false.
An ordinary notification obeys NotificationsEnabled; an explicit preview can use
`Preview = true`. Confirm defaults: Title `Are you sure?`, Description empty,
ConfirmText `Confirm`, Text unset, ReadOnly false and no callbacks/validator.

## Reset defaults versus saved configs

`CaptureDefaults()` captures the **current UI profile**, not this JSON catalog.
Build every control, capture once, then configure persistence. `Reset('All')`
returns to that captured baseline and does not delete configs. `RequestReset`
adds the normal in-product confirmation. An app can deliberately capture Forest
as its baseline without changing the library's factory Light default.

The demo's named `Default` config is a separately saved snapshot. Its presence
does not change what CaptureDefaults means. Saved startup state/auto-load overrides
construction values. A custom accent stays custom across themes until ResetAccent.

## Persistence and schemas

Persistence starts disabled. Ready() captures defaults and creates a named Default
config; with no adapter it reports Session only. Ready({Adapter=adapter,Key="settings"})
also configures storage (default key settings). ConfigurePersistence is the lower-level
API and needs Adapter and Key;
AutoSave true, Load true, Debounce 1.5 seconds. It polls at 0.5 seconds and retries
failed writes after 6 seconds. Save must return true after acknowledgement.
Initial load failure blocks writes until recovery. Server key limit is 24 bytes
(core limit 64); full document limit 200,000 bytes. Server cooldown is 6 seconds.

Config names trim whitespace, require 1–32 UTF-8 characters, at most 128 bytes,
no control characters and no case-insensitive duplicates. Limit: 20 configs per
scope, 32 scopes, 50,000-byte profile, 100,000-byte transfer. Auto-load starts unset.
Layout/profile/settings/transfer schema versions are 1. Transfer Kind is
`PearlUIConfig`; it contains Name, Scope and Profile. See [Configs](Configs.md)
and [Persistence](Persistence.md) for exact flows and legacy migration.

## Theme palette

Light, Dark, Midnight, Graphite, Lavender, Rose, Matcha, Ocean, Forest.
The catalog contains every palette's Window, Sidebar, Card, Text, Muted, Border,
Track, Field, Hover and Accent HEX values, generated directly from the module.
Light accent is #0071F6; Forest accent is #37744A.

The showcase is an opinionated app, not a factory-value fixture: game scope,
enabled notification toggle, selected favorite tools, and its narrower 0.05–0.5
animation slider are deliberate overrides recorded in demoOverrides in the catalog.

The demo now has **7 tabs, 14 sections and 102 initial controls**. The original
General, Appearance, Controls and Profiles tabs remain available. Three new
tabs expose every public method in the library for hands-on inspection.

## Components

**All components** contains Toggle, stepped Slider, searchable single and
multiple Dropdowns, a dropdown without search, ColorPicker with alpha, Input,
Keybind with an OnPressed result, Button and Label.

**Control inspector** selects a target and runs Get, Serialize, Set, silent Set,
OnChanged attach/remove, CanInteract, enable/disable, show/hide, label changes,
Close, Destroy and Recreate. It shows the latest value, callback count and
action result. False and nil are displayed as values, not failures.

Dropdown actions replace options and open the selected editor. Color actions
read color/alpha, open the editor, set alpha and set HSV. Opening an editor
scrolls its target into view. Use Recreate selected to bring back a control
you deliberately destroyed.

## Window lab

Adjust scale, opacity, desired columns and size, including custom corner
resizing. Test a two-second hide, minimize, maximize, left/right dock stowing
and dock recovery. Select any main-demo section to detach, reveal or dock it;
Dock all brings sections home. Jump between tabs, refresh the user card and
change the menu key. Drag the normal title bars, resize grip and dock directly
to inspect pointer behavior.

## API tools

Open an isolated **Pearl sample** window to test construction and destruction.
Drag its title bar aside if it covers the main inspector. The sample has its
own value, captured defaults and reset confirmation. Closing/destroying it
does not destroy the main demo. Destroying the main demo disposes the sample.

Connect sample memory storage, save, toggle its value and reload to inspect a
real adapter roundtrip without touching your own configuration files. The
sample config menu covers create/save/load/rename/delete, startup selection,
listing/status, export/validate/import, legacy profiles and observer
subscription/disconnection. Start by creating the sample config before
running operations that require one. Export to the sample buffer before
validating or importing that buffer.

Data & feedback opens main layout/profile JSON and recent action results,
lists themes, demonstrates sample JSON restoration, notifications,
confirmation/cancellation and a text editor, and previews theme/accent changes.
Parameter controls track changes made elsewhere in the demo silently.

## Coverage

[ShowcaseAPI.json](ShowcaseAPI.json) maps **all 81 public methods** to visible
controls/actions. Factories are represented by the live component examples
and the Open sample action. This map was checked against the public functions
in src/PearlUI.luau, including dropdown/color-specific methods.

The private underscore methods are implementation details and are not listed
as public test actions. Showcase control values are marked Persist=false;
ordinary window/theme settings and real Profiles actions retain their normal
persistence behavior. Sample storage is memory-only and uses a separate
sample window/config scope.

For integration, put examples/Showcase.luau into ReplicatedStorage as a
ModuleScript named PearlUIShowcase and run:

```lua
window._testBench = require(showcaseModule)(PearlUI, window)
```

The generated Studio place, Rojo project and standalone client already include
this integration. The runtime showcase suite validates coverage and core
interactive paths; native touch/gamepad and every manual action sequence have
not been tested.

pages.markdown:
## Local checks

Run from the repository root:

```text
python tools/build.py
python tools/sync_skill.py
python tools/validate_metadata.py
python skills/pearl-ui/scripts/inspect_project.py .
```

Build checks exact embedded-source roundtrips in generated XML. Metadata validation
checks all public API signatures/contracts, all theme roles and default constraints,
showcase coverage, copied skill references and portable links. It does not emulate
Roblox GUI behavior. Compile changed Luau using an available official luau-compile;
compiler success is syntax validation, not a Roblox runtime test.

## Runtime suites

Run test ModuleScripts on a disposable client UI with the same library version,
not a live window containing someone’s real configs. Most return a function taking
`PearlUI`: Runtime, Animation, Dock, Features, FeatureMotion, ColumnsProfile, Audit,
DetachedGeometry, NotificationDock, Themes, Settings and Configs. Each throws on
failure and returns results after cleanup. Read the suite body for its prerequisites.
FileStorage takes the file-adapter factory and provides fake storage. PersistenceServer
takes a build function that evaluates the server with mocked services; it does not
validate a published DataStore. Showcase takes `build` (fresh complete demo factory)
and the public method-name array from docs/API.json, exposing `_testBench` internally.

When a connected-client tool is available, list clients and select the intended
session afresh; never store client identifiers in source/skill. Load exact source
without altering newlines or escaping, check syntax/evaluation responses, run suites
against isolated test instances and destroy them. A disconnect ends that run; reconnect
and re-list before continuing. Do not touch an unrelated game's remotes or reset a
person's saved configs to make a test pass.

## Regression coverage to choose

- Controls/value validation/ID rollback: Runtime, Features, Audit.
- Layout, responsive columns, profile roundtrip: ColumnsProfile, DetachedGeometry.
- Overlapping motion/theme/opacity: Animation, FeatureMotion, NotificationDock, Themes.
- Dock position/stow/recovery: Dock and native viewport/input checks.
- Reset/config/storage: Settings, Configs, FileStorage, PersistenceServer as applicable.
- Showcase bindings and every API location: Showcase and metadata coverage.

Native visual checks should include both themes and custom accents, rapid tab/open/
close/detach/dock actions, popup clipping, scroll bounds, compact viewport, disabled
controls, preview toast and side-stowed dock recovery. Record what was actually tried.

## Current 1.0.2 rerun audit

The replacement patch passed 379 assertions across eight suites: Rerun, Runtime,
Audit, Settings, Configs, Release, Close and Showcase. A separately evaluated
module retired the prior owner, flushed mock storage and restored values in the
new instance. Concurrent replacement and the 1.0.1 legacy upgrade were checked.
The real remote example was evaluated three times: one main window and one dock
remained, with both old owners and their listeners retired. See
[RerunValidation.json](../tests/RerunValidation.json) for provenance and limits.
Fixtures intentionally comparing multiple same-name windows opt out with
ReplaceExisting=false. Do not opt out in ordinary rerun tests.

## Previous 1.0.1 close-button audit

The close-button patch passed 108 assertions: Close 20, Settings 38 and Runtime 50.
Red confirms complete teardown; Cancel retains the UI and yellow only minimizes.
Desktop and touch hit targets share one action. See
[CloseValidation.json](../tests/CloseValidation.json) for scope and provenance.
The full 1.0.0 audit below is historical for this patch, not a fresh full rerun.

## Previous 1.0.0 evidence

The release audit passed 587 assertions across 16 suites plus the separate Icons
construction suite (2,029 icons / 301 runtime aliases). See
[ReleaseValidation.json](../tests/ReleaseValidation.json) for exact commit provenance.
After the final native color-inset correction, Features, FeatureMotion and Release
were rerun successfully; unrelated suites retain the preceding full-run results.
Native mouse checks confirmed color changes, Done, dropdown page navigation and
selection from a rebuilt page. Compact viewport and gamepad cases are simulated.

Run `python tools/check.py --compiler <luau-compile> --verify-generated` for the
reproducible build, geometry, metadata and syntax checks. GitHub Actions runs the
same checks using a checksum-pinned official compiler on each push/PR. This CI
does not emulate a Roblox client. Physical touch/controller hardware, a published
DataStore and reopening XML in Studio remain unverified.

## Historical evidence boundaries

The 0.8.0 audit recorded 45 passing showcase checks; its historical
0.7.0 core baseline is 424 checks across 14 suites. The baseline was not rerun for
the demo-only update. These are separate results, not 469 fresh 0.8.0 checks.
Published DataStore, physical touch/gamepad and reopening generated XML in Studio
remain unverified in that report. Local source/build/default documentation checks
must be reported separately from runtime checks. Do not claim new runtime results
from historical counts, static metadata or successful compilation.

ColorPicker.Get.contract: Color plus alpha. Use Serialize for a JSON-safe representation.

ColorPicker.Open.contract: Open SV/hue/alpha and HEX/RGB editor if interactive and visible.

ColorPicker.SetAlpha.contract: Alpha in [0,1], optional silent. Preserve current HEX.

ColorPicker.SetHSV.contract: All channels finite in [0,1], optional silent; validates all channels before applying.

Control.CanInteract.contract: Own destroyed/disabled/visible/row state. Not a complete ancestor visibility or clipping check.

Control.Close.contract: Close an owned dropdown/color editor if open.

Control.Destroy.contract: Idempotent removal, listener/tween cleanup and Id release. Rebuild with the same Id after destruction.

Control.Get.contract: Defensive copy for table values. ColorPicker overrides this to return Color3,alpha.

Control.OnChanged.contract: Replace callback; nil removes it. This is one callback slot, not an event subscription list.

Control.Serialize.contract: ColorPicker returns {Hex,Alpha}; multi-dropdown returns an array. Never serialize GUI instances.

Control.Set.contract: Validate, store and render. Callback fires unless silent=true; works while disabled. Destroyed controls reject setters.

Control.SetDisabled.contract: Boolean plus optional reason. Blocks native input and cancels owned popup/capture/drag; setters still work.

Control.SetIcon.contract: Set or remove a Lucide label-side icon on any control, without changing its value, Id or callback. nil removes it.

Control.SetLabel.contract: Change presentation without changing Id; refresh search matching.

Control.SetVisible.contract: Hide/show while respecting search. Hiding closes owned interactions.

Dropdown.Open.contract: Open if enabled and in a visible window/page; multi selection stays open until Done/Close.

Dropdown.SetOptions.contract: Validate new options before mutation; retain valid selections unless default supplied. Third argument silent suppresses callback.

PearlUI.GetThemes.contract: Ordered defensive copy: Light, Dark, Midnight, Graphite, Lavender, Rose, Matcha, Ocean, Forest.

PearlUI.new.contract: Client constructor; LocalScript or explicit Parent. ReplaceExisting=true retires PearlUI owners with the same Name/Parent across module reloads; false permits duplicates. Invalid options preserve the old UI; overlapping replacements error while closing. Enum KeyCode for constructor ToggleKey.

Section.Button.contract: Text='Run', Primary=false. Callback() on activation. No persistence Id/value contract.

Section.ColorPicker.contract: Default current accent, Alpha=1. Accept Color3, HEX or {Hex,Alpha}; callback receives Color3,alpha.

Section.Detach.contract: Move card to a floating window, resetting card origin/canvas. Already detached reveals it.

Section.Dock.contract: Return content synchronously to its own page; fade empty floating shell independently.

Section.Dropdown.contract: Required nonempty unique string Options. Multi=false, Searchable=true, PageSize=50 (10..100). Search covers all options; render one bounded page. Scalar or ordered array value.

Section.Input.contract: Default empty string; MaxLength=128 UTF-8 characters, Placeholder='Enter text'. Commits on focus loss.

Section.Keybind.contract: Default RightShift. Callback(string key name) for changes; OnPressed(Enum.KeyCode) for activation.

Section.Label.contract: String shorthand or {Label,Value}; Value defaults empty. Get/Set useful for result labels; no persistence Id.

Section.Reveal.contract: Reveal/focus detached panel, restoring hidden/minimized main window; detaches if needed.

Section.SetIcon.contract: Replace section header icon, including detached panels. nil restores grip-vertical.

Section.Slider.contract: Finite numeric Min/Max/Step; defaults 0/100/1; clamped and quantized value, Callback(number).

Tab.Section.contract: String or {Title, Id, Column, Icon}. Stable unique Id; Column Left/Right, alternating by default; Icon defaults grip-vertical.

Tab.SetIcon.contract: Replace sidebar and dock icon together; preserve current selection and theme bindings.

Window.CaptureDefaults.contract: Capture current profile after building UI and before loading user state. Named Default profile is separate.

Window.ConfigurePersistence.contract: Adapter Load/Save, Key required; AutoSave=true, Load=true, Debounce=1.5, optional OnStatus. Configure after CaptureDefaults.

Window.Confirm.contract: Title/Description/ConfirmText/OnConfirm/OnCancel. Optional Text, ReadOnly and Validate for editor. Handle Confirm/Cancel complete once; Editor/ErrorLabel available for inspection.

Window.CreateConfig.contract: Capture current profile under a new normalized name; set active; reject duplicates/capacity overflow.

Window.DeleteConfig.contract: Remove snapshot, clear matching references; do not reset current values. UI wraps this with confirmation.

Window.Destroy.contract: Idempotent teardown; attempt final auto-save, cancel jobs/tweens/listeners, dispose both ScreenGuis. Showcase also disposes its sample.

Window.DisablePersistence.contract: flush=true attempts SaveSettings first; false disconnects without a write. Cancels its watcher.

Window.ExportConfig.contract: One versioned PearlUIConfig envelope with Name, Scope and Profile, not all configs.

Window.ExportProfile.contract: Version=1, Values, Appearance and Layout. Persist=false controls and destroyed controls are excluded.

Window.Focus.contract: Open/restore the window and focus a control or owned GuiObject. Omit target to focus current popup/modal/page; requires GamepadNavigation=true.

Window.GetConfigStatus.contract: Scope, Active, AutoLoad, Dirty, Count. Manager fields and transient tab/visibility changes do not create edited status.

Window.GetLayout.contract: Version=1 layout with Window, Dock, Panels and ActiveTab; normalized positions, no GUI objects.

Window.GetPersistenceStatus.contract: Disabled, Ready, Loading, Unsaved, Saving, Saved or Error.

Window.ImportConfig.contract: Save a validated copy into current scope without applying; overwrite=true explicitly replaces an exact name.

Window.ImportLayout.contract: Validate table or JSON before applying window, tab, panel and dock geometry.

Window.ImportProfile.contract: Validate known control values/appearance/layout before applying; legacy AccentMode omission retains custom-color behavior.

Window.ListConfigs.contract: Sorted defensive list for current scope.

Window.LoadConfig.contract: Apply named profile and set active only on success.

Window.LoadProfile.contract: Legacy raw named-profile apply. Prefer LoadConfig for active-config tracking.

Window.LoadSettings.contract: Load/validate current game bank and named configs; selected auto-load overrides last working setup. Failed load blocks writes.

Window.Notify.contract: String shorthand or {Title,Description,Duration,Preview}. Disabled preference suppresses ordinary notifications; Preview=true bypasses it without changing preference.

Window.OnConfigsChanged.contract: Observe list/metadata changes. This is not a callback for every control edit.

Window.Ready.contract: After building UI, capture defaults once, optionally create Default config and configure Adapter/Key/Load/AutoSave/Debounce/OnStatus. No adapter reports Session only. Repeated successful calls preserve current edits; failed loading can be retried.

Window.RefreshUserProfile.contract: Refresh LocalPlayer display name, username and AvatarBust thumbnail, with fallback/token guards.

Window.RenameConfig.contract: Move snapshot; update active/auto-load references; preserve current values.

Window.RequestReset.contract: Same scopes, with an in-product confirmation before application.

Window.Reset.contract: Apply captured Appearance/Controls/Layout/All immediately; requires CaptureDefaults and keeps named configs.

Window.ResetAccent.contract: Return to Theme mode; later themes follow their own accents. Demo also synchronizes its picker.

Window.RevealDock.contract: Reveal expanded dock from edge; immediate=true skips its travel tween. Does not open main by itself.

Window.SaveConfig.contract: Update existing named snapshot from current setup and set active. Does not mean adapter has already acknowledged disk save.

Window.SaveProfile.contract: Legacy named save in current scope; uses storage-budget checks. With persistence configured it survives through the settings envelope.

Window.SaveSettings.contract: Save latest current setup and banks only after acknowledged adapter write; skip unchanged snapshot.

Window.SelectTab.contract: Tab object belonging to window or known name; closes menu and updates active page/search.

Window.SetAccent.contract: Color3 sets Custom accent mode. nil restores the selected theme's accent.

Window.SetAutoLoadConfig.contract: Known name selects startup snapshot; nil clears it for this scope.

Window.SetColumns.contract: Only 1 or 2. Effective columns may collapse to one for a narrow viewport.

Window.SetMinimized.contract: Minimize/restore; separate from Visible and from dock stow side.

Window.SetOpacity.contract: Finite number, clamped to [0.75,1], including surfaces with a visibility transition.

Window.SetScale.contract: Finite desired scale clamped to [0.65,1.3]; actual fit scale may be smaller.

Window.SetSize.contract: Finite width/height; rounded, clamped to 680x420..1440x1000, with viewport fitting.

Window.SetTheme.contract: Name from GetThemes. Repaint all bound roles while preserving a custom accent override.

Window.SetToggleKey.contract: Enum.KeyCode or key-name string; updates footer. Constructor itself expects an Enum.KeyCode.

Window.SetVisible.contract: Show/hide main and detached panels; hidden main leaves the dock available.

Window.StowDock.contract: Left or Right; hides dock offscreen with recovery handle, retaining height.

Window.Tab.contract: String or {Name, Description, Icon}. Adds sidebar and dock entries; first tab is selected.

Window.ValidateConfig.contract: Validate package or legacy profile JSON without applying or storing it.
